title: Her lost birth certificate and the 1901 date
summary: Her certificate burned in a courthouse fire and the census bureau assigned 1901, about three years too early.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: You know, I'm not that old.
You know, I'm not that old.
You know, I'm not that old. I was born the 29th of March because my mother told me, but my birthday certificate got burned up. Who put it in 1901?
They were a census bureau. They had to make me a one.

Oh, oh. So that's what it is, see. But they didn't make it. But I had to go buy it because I didn't have nothing else to go buy it. I had to get my license, you see. So that's why I had to have it. So that's what's on your license? I don't know.

Got me 1901, that's what they got me. Yeah. But I knew I'm not that old. No, I'm not that old. There was nothing I could do about it. See, I had wrote two Washington and bought my birthday certificate. In fact, I had sent for Jacksonville because I would have sent that first because that's the capital. But they told me that they used to keep all the birthday certificates in Pensacola in the court house. Well the court house caught a fire. And that book got burnt up where they had the numbers in it. They didn't have it. So when I wrote to Washington, they told me to write to the census bureau they would make me up something. They made me up something all right. But they didn't make up. Really they got me around three years older than what I am, see.
Sometimes the state keeps the record too so they might have that in Tallahassee.
Most states they do, they record it. The state capital too.
